description_text: The Panzerkampfwagen 38(t) was a conventional pre-World War II tank design, with riveted armor and rear engine. It was a Czechoslovakian tank and was named TNHP-S. After the invasion of Czechoslovakia by German forces, the tank was adopted by the German Army due to insufficient production of German tanks to meet the war requirement.  It was called the Panzerkampfwagen 38(t), with 38 signifying the year of introduction and t for Tschechisch, meaning Czech in German. Over 1,400 units were manufactured until 1942, where it saw extensive service in France and then the Russian front, namely in the Battle of Kursk in the summer of 1942.  The riveted construction of the tank made it different from German-made tanks. While riveted design was simpler and cheaper than welded steel, but a direct hit from an antitank round was usually fatal for the crew as the rivets bolted out acting as deadly projectiles.  Armament consisted of a 37mm main gun with 42 rounds and two machine guns (one mounted coaxially on the turret and the other in the front hull). Power was supplied by a Praga EPA 125hp engine.

description_text: The T-24 was a Soviet medium tank built in 1931. Only twenty-four tanks were built, and saw no combat. This was the first tank produced at the KhPZ factory in Ukraine, which was later responsible for the very successful T-34 and T-54 Soviet tanks. The T-24's suspension was used successfully in the Soviet Union's first purpose-built artillery tractors.   The T-24's main armament was a 45 mm gun. It had a ball-mount 7.62 mm DT machine gun in the hull, another in the turret, and a third in a secondary turret atop the main turret. The tank was well-armoured for its time, but suffered from problems with the engine and transmission.

description_text: The Iosif Stalin tank (or IS tank, named after the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin) was a heavy tank developed by the Soviet Union during World War II. The tanks in the series are also sometimes called JS or ИС tanks.   The heavy tank was designed with thick armour to counter the German 88 mm guns, and carried a main gun that was capable of defeating the German Tiger and Panther tanks. It was mainly a breakthrough tank, firing a heavy high-explosive shell that was useful against entrenchments and bunkers. In late 1944 the design was upgraded to the IS-3. This tank had improved armour layout, and a hemispherical cast turret (resembling an overturned soup bowl) which became the hallmark of post-war Soviet tanks. While this low, hemispherical turret may have made the IS-3 better protected, it also imposed severe penalties inside the tank by significantly diminishing the working headroom, especially for the loader (Soviet tanks in general are characterized by uncomfortably small interior space compared to Western tanks).

description_text: A light reconnaissance tank, the Ausf. L was the only Panzer II design with the overlapping road wheels to enter series production, with 100 being built from September 1943 to January 1944 in addition to conversion of the four Ausf. M tanks. Originally given the experimental designation VK1303, it was adopted under the alternate name Panzerspähwagen II and given the popular name Luchs (Lynx). The Lynx was larger than the Ausf. G in most dimensions (length 4.63 m; height 2.21 m; width 2.48 m). It was equipped with a six speed transmission (plus reverse), and could reach a speed of 60 km/h with a range of 290 km. The FuG12 and FuG Spr a radios were installed, while 330 rounds of 20 mm and 2,250 rounds of 7.92 mm ammunition were carried. Total vehicle weight was 13 tons.  This armored vehicle was modeled in cooperation between TOBY and me.

description_text: The Panzer I was a light tank produced in Germany in the 1930s. The name is short for the German Panzerkampfwagen I (armored fighting vehicle mark I), abbreviated PzKpfw I. Design of the Panzer I began in 1932 and mass production in 1934. Intended only as a training tank to introduce the concept of armored warfare to the German Army, the Panzer I saw combat in Spain during the Spanish Civil War, in Poland, France, the Soviet Union and North Africa during the Second World War. Experiences with the Panzer I during the Spanish Civil War helped shape the German armored corps' invasion of Poland in 1939 and France in 1940. By 1941, the Panzer I chassis design was used for production of tank destroyers and assault guns. There were attempts to upgrade the Panzer I throughout its service history, including by foreign nations to extend the design lifespan. It continued to serve in the armed forces of Spain until 1954.  The Panzer I's performance in combat was limited by its thin armor and light armament of two general purpose machine guns.  Although weak in combat, it formed a large portion of Germany's tank strength in numbers and was used in all major campaigns between September 1939 and December 1941. The small, vulnerable light tank would be surpassed in importance by better-known German tanks. Nevertheless, the Panzer I's contribution to the early victories of Nazi Germany during the Second World War was significant.

description_text: The Panzerkampfwagen 35(t), commonly shortened to Panzer 35(t) or abbreviated as Pz.Kpfw. 35(t), was a Czech-designed light tank used mainly by Nazi Germany during World War II. The letter (t) stood for tschechisch (German: Czech). In Czech service it had the formal designation Lehký (Light) Tank vzor (Model) 35, but was commonly referred to as the LT vz. 35. Four hundred and thirty-four were built; of these the Germans seized two hundred and forty-four when they occupied Bohemia-Moravia in March 1939 and the Slovaks acquired fifty-two when they declared independence from Czechoslovakia at the same time. Others were exported to Bulgaria and Romania. In German service it saw combat during the early years of World War II, notably the Invasion of Poland, the Battle of France and the invasion of the Soviet Union before being retired or sold off in 1942. It was used for the remainder of the war by other countries and as a training tank in Bulgaria into the 1950s.

description_text: Panzer II was the common name of a German tank used in World War II. The official German designation was Panzerkampfwagen II (abbreviated PzKpfw II). Designed as a stopgap while other tanks were developed, it played an important role in the early years of World War II, during the Polish and French campaigns. By the end of 1942, it was largely removed from frontline service and production of the tank itself ceased by 1943, but its chassis was used for several other armored vehicles.     Most tank versions of the Panzer II were armed with a 2 cm KwK 30 55 calibers long cannon. Some later versions used the 2 cm KwK 38 L/55 which was similar. This cannon was based on the 2 cm FlaK 30 anti-aircraft gun, and was capable of firing at a rate of 280 rounds per minute, a very high rate for a tank. The Panzer II also had a 7.92 mm Maschinengewehr 34 machine gun mounted coaxially with the main gun.

description_text: The Panzer III was intended as the primary battle tank of the German forces. However, when it initially met the KV and T-34 tanks it proved to be inferior in both armor and gun power. To meet the growing need to counter these tanks, the Panzer III was up-gunned with a longer, more powerful 50-millimetre (1.97 in) cannon and received more armour although this failed to effectively address the problem caused by the KV tank designs. As a result, production of self-propelled guns, as well as the up-gunning of the Panzer IV was initiated.The Ausf. F were upgraded with the 5 cm KwK 38 L/42 cannon in response to increasingly better armed and armoured opponents.This version is earlier than my other model.

Ausf A was produced from July of 1934 to June of 1936 , while Ausf B was produced from August of 1935 to June of 1937. Both were produced by Henschel, MAN, Krupp-Gruson and Daimler-Benz. Ausf A proved to be underpowered and its very loud 57hp Krupp engine overheated and Ausf B with its 100hp Maybach engine was an improved version of Ausf A (See my other model). Both models had identical turret and superstructure but Ausf B was longer (additional roadwheel) and had new modified engine deck (new engine). Both variants were operated by two men crew - a driver and a commander/gunner. The main armament consisted of two 7.92mm MG13 Dreyse (medium) machine guns with rate of fire of 650 rounds per minute.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Development of the Marder series of self-propelled anti-tank guns in late 1941 to increase the mobility of anti-tank weapons by mounting them on a variety of available chassis. The Germans saw a need for this vehicle type following the appearance of new Russian armoured fighting vehicles, especially the T-34 series of medium tanks and the heavy KV series. Vehicles of the Marder series were based on proven chassis of obsolete tanks, as well as on those of captured vehicles. In all cases, the main armament had a limited traverse, forcing the vehicle to change its position to face the enemy and aim the gun.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Sometimes known as the Bison. The larger Ausf B chassis made possible the mounting of heavier guns with removal of the turret. The largest was the 150 mm heavy infantry gun, the sIG 33. This mammoth piece was relatively short and fit just barely in a tall superstructure not only built up to the vehicle's 2.8 m height but also out over the tracks to their full 2.06 m width. The superstructure armor was light at only 13 mm and only protected the front and sides. The heavy resulting weight of 8.5 tons overstressed the chassis and ultimately, the vehicle was not a great success. 38 were converted from Ausf B tanks in February 1940 and they served with six heavy SP infantry gun companies with survivors in service into 1943. The sIG mounting was capable of 25 ° of traverse and 75 ° of elevation, and could be depressed to -4 °. It used a Rblf36 sight, and ammunition was carried separately, there being no room for onboard shell storage. The sIG would be mounted more successfully on larger chassis as the war progressed.

description_text: The Panzerjäger I (German Tank Hunter 1) was the first of the German tank destroyers to see service in the Second World War. It mounted a Czech Skoda 47 mm (1.9 in) cm PaK (t) anti-tank gun on a converted Panzer I Ausf. B chassis. It was intended to counter heavy French tanks like the Char B1 that were beyond the capabilities of the 37 mm PaK 36 anti-tank gun then in service and served to extend the usable lifetime of otherwise obsolete Panzer I tanks. Over 200 were converted in 1940—41. They were employed in the Battle of France, in the North Africa Campaign and on the Eastern Front.

Napoleón I Bonaparte (Ajaccio, 15 de agosto de 1769-Longwood, 5 de mayo de 1821) fue un militar y estadista francés, general republicano durante la Revolución francesa y el Directorio, y artífice del golpe de Estado del 18 de brumario que lo convirtió en primer cónsul (Premier Consul) de la República el 11 de noviembre de 1799. Fue además cónsul vitalicio desde el 2 de agosto de 1802 hasta su proclamación como emperador de los franceses el 18 de mayo de 1804, siendo coronado el 2 de diciembre; fue proclamado también rey de Italia el 18 de marzo de 1805 y coronado el 26 de mayo. Ostentó ambos títulos hasta el 11 de abril de 1814, y desde el 20 de marzo hasta el 22 de junio de 1815.

Scale armour is an early form of armour consisting of many individual small armour scales (plates) of various shapes attached to each other and to a backing of cloth or leather in overlapping rows.[1] Scale armour was worn by warriors of many different cultures as well as their horses. The material used to make the scales varied and included bronze, iron, rawhide, leather, cuir bouilli, seeds, horn, pangolin scales and, in ancient China, paper. The variations are primarily the result of material availability.Scale armour is armour in which the individual scales are sewn or laced to a backing by one or more edges and arranged in overlapping rows resembling the scales of a fish/reptile or roofing tiles.[2] Lorica squamata is an ancient Roman armour of this type[1] and gyorin kozane is the Japanese (samurai) name for this type of scale armour.[3]Other types of armours made from individual scales but constructed in a different manner have their own separate names such as lamellar armour where the individual scales are perforated on several or all edges and lashed tightly to each other in straight ridged rows and do not need to be attached to a backing. The Romans also had a variant called lorica plumata in which the scales were attached to mail.[4]

If you have other questions regarding 3d printing, you can contact us without hesitate. If for any reason, any of the supplied files does not work for you,no problem, get in touch and we will validate and if you require an update of the files with pleasure and without additional cost we will do it.

Berserk
A Man's a Man for A' That
Is there for honest PovertyThat hings his head, an' a' that;The coward slave-we pass him by,We dare be poor for a' that!For a' that, an' a' that.Our toils obscure an' a' that,The rank is but the guinea's stamp,The Man's the gowd for a' that.
What though on hamely fare we dine,Wear hodden grey, an' a that;Gie fools their silks, and knaves their wine;A Man's a Man for a' that:For a' that, and a' that,Their tinsel show, an' a' that;The honest man, tho' e'er sae poor,Is king o' men for a' that.
Ye see yon birkie, ca'd a lord,Wha struts, an' stares, an' a' that;Tho' hundreds worship at his word,He's but a coof for a' that:For a' that, an' a' that,His ribband, star, an' a' that:The man o' independent mindHe looks an' laughs at a' that.
A prince can mak a belted knight,A marquis, duke, an' a' that;But an honest man's abon his might,Gude faith, he maunna fa' that!For a' that, an' a' that,Their dignities an' a' that;The pith o' sense, an' pride o' worth,Are higher rank than a' that.
Then let us pray that come it may,(As come it will for a' that,)That Sense and Worth, o'er a' the earth,Shall bear the gree, an' a' that.For a' that, an' a' that,It's coming yet for a' that,That Man to Man, the world o'er,Shall brothers be for a' that.
1795

description_text: The 128 mm Selbstfahrlafette Sturer Emil was an experimental World War II German self-propelled anti-tank gun. It was based on the Henschel VK3001 chassis and armed with a Rheinmetall 128 mm K L/61 gun (based on the 12.8 cm FlaK 40). This gun could traverse 7° to each side, elevate 10° and depress 15°. It carried 18 rounds for the main gun.   The chassis was left over from Henschel's submission for the canceled VK3001 heavy tank program, but the hull was stretched and an extra road wheel added to accommodate the large gun, which was mounted on a pedestal ahead of the engine. A large, open-topped, fighting compartment was built where the turret was intended to go in the original design.   Two vehicles (named Max and Moritz) were built, both of which served on the Eastern Front. One vehicle was destroyed, the other captured at Stalingrad in January 1943, with 11 kill marks painted on the barrel. This captured vehicle is now displayed in the collection on the Kubinka Tank Museum.  This Tank was made in cooperation between TOBY and me.

description_text:
Sci Fi Grenade low-poly model optimized for Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), games and other real-time apps. Created with Cinema4D R17 and final images rendered in Octane. The model comes with the textures in .png format / 16 bits.
The pack contains 4 variations of the grenade. Offensive / Chemical / Flash / Smoke.All the variations are made on the diffuse map with 4 diferent colors to differentiate them. Every diffuse map are not the same, some icon variations and typography change as you can see in the previewer. Textured in 3DO with Quixel suite.
Model description: 

  - Geometry: Quad/tris 

  - Polygon count: 1168 (Quads version) / 2238 (Low poly) / 4642 (Low poly V2) - - 

  - The are 3 diferents polygon count model version

  - Objects: 1

  - Uv mapped: Yes 

  - Unwrapped UVs: Yes-non overlapping 

  - Textures: Yes 

  - Textures file: .PNG 

  - Texture size: 4096*4096

File formats: 

  - 3d model.3ds 

  - 3d model.obj 

  - 3d model.stl 

  - 3d model.dae 

  - 3d model.fbx

Features: 

  - Optimized for game engine with PBR shader.

  - There are no pluggins needed to open the scene. 

  - Unique design made with love! 

  - 4 diffuse map variations of the grenade 

  - 4K textures great for close up render. 

  - 3 diferents polygon count model in all format.

  - Real size model. 

  - The model is centered at origin and ready to go.

Note: The scene settings (cameras, lights, etc ) are not included. You may have to link the png texture files.If you have any questions please feel free to ask.
Thanks for viewing! Dretkp

description_text:
The model you see currently is a chopping axe. It is a great tool for chopping logs and heads (if you're a crazy person, so am I). The model is made so that it has been used a lot, you can see the wood has some scratches and starts to become darker with time, and the blade starts to be rusty.
By buying the asset, you'll get access to two types of model. A classic one, and a game-ready one.-The classic one is a sudbivision-ready asset, meaning you can add an unlimited number of subdivision without destroying the model (but you might break your computer), with an increasing level of detail if you prefer to have a closer look of the model. Above, you can see multiple wireframe views, respectively without sudbivision, with a level 1 subdivision, and a level 2 subdivision. Without subdivision, the model has 728 faces. You can also remove some edge loops if you really want to have your model on point and as optimized as possible.-The game-ready one is a ultra-light version of the model, optimized for video games or in 3D scenes where the polycount has to be as low as possible. This one has 295 faces.
The model comes with 2 different sets of textures. One set is for the classic model, and the other one is for the game-ready asset.Each set comes with 4096x4096, 2048x2048, 1024x1024 and 512x512 textures.Diffuse, Roughness, Normal, Metallic, AO, and Height.
Here are the different formats : .obj (with its .mtl file), .fbx, .stl, .3ds and .abc .You also have a .blend file with the asset, so you can have access to the node settings, and the scene used to make the renders.
The model has been created in Blender 2.79 and rendered in Cycles, textured in Substance Painter, and some post-process has been done in the Blender Compositor.
Please note : This model is not printable. Don't expect it to work, I strongly advise you not to purchase the model if you intend to print it, as it could end with unexpected results.If you have any question, recommandation, or if you're in trouble, feel free to send me a message so I can help you out.Good chopping!

Should interest be shown, future packs will certainly be coming!

description_text:
A sledgehammer !Be ready to demolish walls and put some pillars in the dirt. But, in my opinion, it's much better when used to bash an enemy's head in video games ! The model is made so that it has been used a lot, you can see the wood starts to become darker with time, and the head of the sledgehammer as a lot of impacts, the paint is scratched and the metal parts are worn.
It is a sudbivision-ready asset, meaning you can add an unlimited number of subdivision without destroying the model (but you might break your computer), with an increasing level of detail if you prefer to have a closer look of the model. Above, you can see multiple wireframe views, respectively without sudbivision, with a level 1 subdivision, and a level 2 subdivision. Without subdivision, the model has 1,495 faces. You can also remove some edge loops if you really want to have your model on point and as optimized as possible.
The model comes with 2 different sets of textures. One set is for the head of the model, and the other one is for the wood pole.

description_text:
The model above is a close representation of a KA-BAR knife. I decided to change the look of the handle a bit (honestly that was because I had a bad reference image and I realized at the end it was not the generic shape). It was widely used by US military forces and marines. It is a great tool for cutting through flesh, for opening cans,  capable of dealing massive bleeding. The model is made so that it has been quite a lot of time, you can see the blade is worn and the handle is scratched.
Technical InformationsBy buying the asset, you'll get full access to the model.The model has been created, bearing in mind that it should be a sudbivision-ready asset, meaning you can add an unlimited number of subdivision without destroying the model, with an increasing level of detail if you prefer to have a closer look of the model. Above, you can see multiple wireframe views, respectively without sudbivision, with a level 1 subdivision, and a level 2 subdivision. Without subdivision, the model has 4,682 polygons. You can also remove some edge loops if you really want to have your model on point and as optimized as possible.
PolycountThe model has been created by bearing in mind that it should be able to be subdivided afterwards without a problem. You can have a nice looking asset whatever the distance of your camera is, by increasing the amount of detail in a non-destructive way. You can also remove some edge loops if you really want to have your model on point and as optimized as possible.
TexturesBy buying the asset you'll get access to 3 sets of texture, one in 4096x4096, one in 2048x2048 and the last one in 1024x1024.
FormatsFor compatibilty reasons, the models available are in different formats. .fbx , .abc , .obj (with a .mtl) , .stl  and .x3d. The native .blend is also included. Because the model is subdivision-ready, you are given a low-poly version of the model that you can subdivide very easily afterwards, and a high-poly version which is exatcly the same but with a Subdivision level of 2 applied.
What is in the download?A .zip archive with all the texture sets inside (4k, 2k, 1k and 512) All the 3D formats mentionned above, including the native .blend
CautionThis model is NOT 3D printable. Don't expect it to work, I strongly advise you not to purchase the model if you intend to print it, as it could end with unexpected results. If you encounter any issue by using the model, feel free to send me a message so I can help you out. Note that by buying this asset you'll get me fatter and I thank you for that.

description_text:
Description:
These swords are based on Danish bog finds from Vimose and Illerup dal. They date to the Third Century CE and, despite being found in Barbaricum, are Roman in manufacture (probably manufactured in Roman Gaul - modern France). Perhaps they were loot from a raid, but more than likely they were brought home after mercenary or auxiliary service in the Roman army. This is a type of sword colloquially known as a 'spatha', which is longer than the common Roman infantry short sword, the 'gladius'. Longer swords were popular within Germanic cultures, and the extra length would have been useful for fighting on horseback.Six texture variants are included with this model. Three 'officer' variants, with gold and silver handle fittings and pattern welded blades; and three 'common' variants with bone and wood hilts and plain steel blades. Three variants of scabbard, all leather with bronze fittings, are also included. The 'officer' variants are based on reconstructions by swordsmith Patrick Barta.
Features:

  - Two low polygon models: sword and scabbard

  - Six texture variants for the swords, three for the scabbard

  - 4096x4096 .png textures for PBR materials, done using a metallic workflow

  - Available as .blend, .fbx, .obj, and .gITF. Other formats available upon request

description_text:
The Cyberzerker clans are some of the toughest  wastelanders in the Great Terrin Basin.  Their halmarks are advanced bionics, genome modification and liberal use of nanite and combat stims whose recipies have been passed down for thousands of years. Bulkers are the heavily augmented remnants of injured shock troopers. They are subjected to extensive mechanical rebuilding, strength boosting, and sent back into the fray as short lived assault units.This kit contains all you need to build a squad of bulkers. Each comes with the option for hammers or blades.
Every part is included with both supported and non-supported versions for ease of printing.Test models were made on an anycubic photon. Printed at 0.05mm layer height Esun's bio-PLA resin (grey) 9.7s standard exposure Models are scaled for 30mm gaming. Parts require support. Recommended resin printing, or FDM with a 0.2mm nozzle.

Model has been created using Blender and Substance Painter. Blender was used for sculpting and retopology Substance painter for texturing.
Workflow used: Created basemesh and then sculpted all the details then retopologized and baked normals from sculpted verison in substance painter. If you need some texture color changes feel free to contact me and it can be done.
Design: This katana is very old but has been refubrished and found its new life in current times!
UVs: most of UV are mirrored to save UV space.
After buying you receive both rigged and unrigged version, note that only rigged part is manekineko charm.
Renders: Video is done using Eevee render engine in Blender rest of images are from cycles render engine in Blender. I also added some render from Substance painter renderer.
If you need any additional details feel free to contact me.
You can see other versions of this model here: https://www.artstation.com/artwork/WKn3mJ
8 438 triangles - Katana
1 074 Triangles Scabbard
This 3d model has been created  to be used in game engine hence it has low poly count with normals baked from hand sculpted version. There is Unity prefab included for concinience with already set up materials uning autodesk shader in Unity 2018.

description_text:
Low poly game-ready medieval longsword that is ready to be dropped into game engines like Unreal Engine or Unity. The model is optimized and triangulated to ensure that it renders the same on both game engines. 
The model has 2380 tris. It comes with 4K PBR textures in TGA format. The model and textures are of a high enough resolution and level of detail to be used either as a hero weapon model or a prop. 
The model is UV unwrapped with non-overlapping UVs. 
Design and dimensions of the model are based on real world longsword references. The model is ideal for any medieval, fantasy or any game you can imagine that uses a longsword! 
The item comes with the following:

  - Longsword.fbx

  - LongswordTextures_4K_TGA.rar (4K TGA textures: Ambient Occlusion, Diffuse, Metallic, Normal, Roughness) 

  - Longsword.blend (Blend file with just the model itself.)

  - Longsword_StudioSetup (Blend file used to render the preview images.)

  - Longsword.obj

  - Longsword.stl

Instructions:

  - Just drag and drop Longsword.fbx into Unreal Engine or Unity and import the PBR textures into your material setup. Obj and stl files are included but I would highly recommend using the fbx file for use in game engines. 

  - For Unreal Engine, you may have to flip the green channel on the normal map setting. 

  - The native file Longsword.blend contains just the model itself with no lighting whatsoever. It is included for you to examine the model or reexport the model into other formats. 

  - The file Longsword_StudioSetup.blend is the lightning setup used to render the preview images above. Just open the file and hit render to see them. 

Thank you for checking the model out. Feel free to contact me if you have any queries or if you require any assistance.

description_text:
Thank you for visiting my bonfire, adventurer!
This pack contains the following models (15 total):

  - Broadsword A and B

  - Curved Sword A, B, and C

  - Dagger A and B

  - Longsword A

  - Greatsword A, B, C, D, and E

  - Ultrasword A and B

MODELSAll models average around 1,500 tris each, with smaller ones being 700 tris and a couple of larger ones at 3,200 tris.There are no LODs included.Each weapon sits at 0,0,0 origin facing upwards, with the pivot at the origin/lowest point of model.In the included MayaLT scene, I added the standard Unreal Engine 4 mannequin as a sizer so you can see the sword sizes as they will appear in-game if you are using UE4.
TEXTURESThere are two texture sets, SwordsA and SwordsB, which can be used with any of the sword models.SwordsA is more realistic and traditional textures. SwordsB are like darker/more gold and bronze, magical, or bloody versions.Both sets have 4096x4096 and 2048x2048 texture maps, so you can choose which one you'd like depending on your type of project.There is a combined map in each of these sets which contain the AO(ambient occlusion) map in channel R, the Roughness map in channel G, and the Metallic map in channel B.I have also included these maps separated as individual ones as well, for more flexibility.
Finally, there are two normal map-types in each texture set. The one with unreal at end of name is used for Unreal Engine, and is created with DirectX.The one with unity at end of name is used for Unity Engine, and is created with OpenGL.

description_text:
Low-poly historical accurate reconstruction of an German executioner’s sword (Richtschwert / Henkerschwert). The oldest known specialized executioner’s swords date back to the end of the 13th century. They were specifically designed to behead or decapitate criminals. They were two-handed swords with a broad blade. They had no point but rather the front was rounded. Additional holes in the front would prevent people from adding a point to the sword. So it was only intended to cut.
**The file includes:**
  - Only the sword with a pear shaped pommel, three holes in the front part and a little symbol of gallows scratched into the blade.
Polys/Verts
  - Sword (1719/1723)
Further Information
Models are:

  - Fully mapped and textured with PBR material (2k).

  - In real world scale (meters).

  - All parts attached together and named.

Realistic game ready low poly one handed weapons ready to be used in any modern game engine.
Model was created in Blender with good topology and optimized polycount in mind. Textures were created in Substance Painter and are fully PBR with resolution up to 4K.

Model has 1852 triangles and 958 vertices.
Model is available in FBX, OBJ.
Topology is clean and optimized for performance in a game engine.

Textures are available in 4k, 2k, and 1k resolution for both PBR Metallic/Roughness and Specular/Glossiness workflows also with Directx and OpenGL normal maps.
I’ve also included textures optimized for Unreal Engine 4.

description_text:
The MK40 missile, a unique Vietnam and Korean war era missile, with FFAR (Folding-Fin Aerial Rocket) design. Primarily used for air-to-ground attack. You can utilize it for your helicopter's rocket pods or for various fun projects. This particular model is designed with the M151 warhead attached to the front of the rocket. The main missile section, warhead, fins, fin pins and nozzle section are each separate objects. The nozzle section (dark gray object) is one piece of geometry with the four nozzles.
Modeled lower poly with added edges to receive subdivision modifiers/proxies. UV unwrapped as non-overlapping. Included in each download are two textures (one for overall color, one for roughness/bump). The Blender download file includes all other file formats available on this listing.

description_text:
Low poly model of Fieseler Fi 103 flying bomb/cruise missile equipped pulse jet engine. Also known as Vergeltungswaffe Eins (V-1) or Vengeance Weapon. Allies called it buzz bomb or doodlebug. This weapon was used by Germany (Third Reich) during World War 2. 
Shape of the model based on free blueprints from Internet. 
Elevator, rudder and propeller are modeled as separate meshes. Simple imitation of the jet engine inner parts and piston in the tail part also modeled. All meshes are triangulated. 
Model includes .blend (native), .obj and .fbx formats. 
Three paint schemes included: two color, spotted and olive with rust spots. 
Every paint scheme composed of PBR textures, two resolutions included for each of them: 2048 and 4096. 
PBR textures contain Base color, AO, Roughness, Metallic and Normal maps (for OpenGL and DirectX). 
Created and rendered in Blender 3.1. Textured in Substance Painter.

Vertices: 6816

description_text:
1/1800th scale Hermes Aircraft Carrier model. Certain elements not to scale.
The HMS Hermes was the first ship designed as an aircraft carrier. She was built shortly after WWI and carried twenty aircraft. She was armed with six five and a half-inch guns and four four-inch guns. She was sunk in 1942 by the Japanese.
This model is designed and tested at 1/1800th scale, but up-scaling and down-scaling are possible. Since the model is optimized for 1/1800th scale, it is not ideal to print larger versions due to a lack of detail. The gun barrels and mast have been enlarged.
This is part of my collection of WWII warships, keep an eye out for more to come. If you have a specific request, message me and I'll bump it up my list.
Update 27 Aug 19: Added boats. Adjustments for better printability.
Tested with PLA at .1mm layer height with .4mm nozzle.

The Soviet RG-42 (   42 > Ruchnaya Granata obraztsa 42 goda, 'Hand Grenade pattern of [19]42 year') was a fragmentation grenade designed by S.G. Korshunov. It was originally introduced during World War II from 1942 onwards as an emergency measure to replace the complex RGD-33 grenade. It continued in use with the USSR and its Warsaw Pact allies in the post-war period until replaced in 1954 by the RGD-5 grenade. Stockpiles were held for emergency or reserve issue, military aid, or foreign sales. They were eventually destroyed in the 1980s due to the TNT filling degrading and becoming unsafe.

description_text:
Clare's Claymore | from the Anime TV Series - Claymore
Claymore swords are large double-edged swords of unknown weight and composition with sharpened hilts. Besides being sharp and strong, the Claymore swords also possess unusually high durability, which suggests that they are not ordinary swords. They seemingly never break or dull.The Claymore Swords have three different variations of colors on the handle. Green is for defensive users. Red is for offensive users. Blue is reserved for the single number digits claymores, So basically any sword from number 10 to number 1 has a blue handle.
I'm quite a fan of this anime series and you have no idea how long I've been waiting to make this model. It comes with no blood on, red blood and purple blood (if you've watched the show, you know where it comes from!).

description_text:
Description
“Zenitsu carries around a standard sized and shaped Nichirin katana with yellow lightning streaks along the entire blade. His sword’s tsuba is circular shaped with 4 slight indentations, the center has a silver tone with small triangles and has a golden border. The handle is yellow and wrapped in white silk ribbon. The base of the handle is gold with two short, white ribbons hanging off it. Along with his katana, Zenitsu also has a standard sword sheath that is white in color.” (https://kimetsu-no-yaiba.fandom.com/wiki/Zenitsu_Agatsuma#Equipment)
As an extra, I've also added a file to the model with a variant of the wraps around the handle for a more realistic style and less anime-ish. You may find a preview of it in the images uploaded (25-32). It should be noted that this variant of the wraps adds roughly more 2K polygons to the overall mesh.

Made Free for my awesome modder friends.The falcata was a curved, two-foot long sword that was used by Celtiberian warriors in ancient Spain.The falcata was a popular type of sword in the Iberian Peninsula from the fifth to the first century B.C.Closely related in form to slashing weapons found in Greece, it is distinguished by the fact that its blade is double-edged for about half of its length.The Kopis was shorter usually a horse-borne sword. Better for lopping at retreating infantry. The Falcata was heftier and longer well suited for breaking shields or other weapons like spears. The Kopis's steep recurve makes thrusts difficult and likely requiring a reverse of grip too thrust in an ergonomic fashion.

description_text:
Realistic game-ready low poly knife in military style. 
The images above are rendered in Blender (Cycles renderer), Unreal Engine and Substance painter and lit by HDRI.
The included texture variants covers your need for both a metallic / roughness and specular / gloss workflow. 
Viable both for picking mushrooms and zombie population control.
4096x4096 (4K) PBR textures included for both Spec/Gloss, Metal/Rough and a packed version for Unreal: Base color, Diffuse, Metallic, Roughness, Specular, Glossiness, Normal, Occlusion and RGB AO/Metal/Rough.
You can import the .uasset files in Unreal to immediately have the model and material set up by simply moving the files into your projects Content folder. Sometimes Unreal breaks some links between the .uasset files so you might have to reassign the material or reselect textures inside the material.

description_text:

The object is scaled according to metric system. The knife is provided with set of 4K textures available in 3 versions dedicated for various usages. Each set contain following maps:

This model is dedicated for video game development, architectural visualisation and cinematics.

description_text:
Club Weapon
A club (also known as a cudgel, baton, bludgeon, truncheon, cosh, nightstick or impact weapon) is among the simplest of all weapons: a short staff or stick, usually made of wood, wielded as a weapon since prehistoric times. There are several examples of blunt-force trauma caused by clubs in the past, including at the site of Nataruk in Turkana, Kenya, described as the scene of a prehistoric conflict between bands of hunter-gatherers 10,000 years ago. In popular culture, clubs are associated with primitive cultures, especially cavemen.

description_text:
This is a typical viking round shield. It is built from wooden planks, has a round, hollow boss made from steel, a rim made out of raw hide, which is sewn through the planks to reinforce the shield. glued to the front side is a layer of linen cloth, which also reinforces the shield and prevents the planks from splintering.The boss and the wooden handle are held in place by iron rivets, the handle is wrapet by leather. This sort of shield is not fastened to the lower arm, it is only held by the handle, so it can swing and deflect blows.

description_text:
Medieval stylised shield
The heater shield or heater-shaped shield is a form of European medieval shield, developing from the early medieval kite shield in the late 12th century as depicted in the great seal of Richard I and John. The term is a neologism, created by Victorian antiquarians due to the shape’s resemblance to a clothes iron.

description_text:
Not suitable for 3D printing
The Buntline Special. A custom Colt Single Action Army revolver, supposedly used by Old West legend Wyatt Earp. Modified with a 12” long barrel, it is supposedly more accurate than typical revolving pistols of that era, provided the wielder could handle the kickback.
Game-ready mesh at semi-low poly count to modern games, modelled to real-world scale. Not suitable for 3D printing.
Comes with: - 2x meshes of the revolver itself, 1 of which is joined into one mesh, the other is in parts according to the breakdown image. (2,948 faces) - 1x .45 caliber bullet in pristine condition. - 1x .45 caliber bullet in spent (fired/burnt) condition without the bullet tip. - Arrangements of 6x both forms of bullet to fit perfectly into the chambers - 1x Ammo box pickup with easy texture editing. - 4x texture image files for each of these meshes (1024 x 1024 px)
All meshes have been game tested by being imported into Unity and work properly, although textures will have to be linked to the relevant materials after import. Any issues please contact me and I'll do my best to resolve it.

Low poly sci-fi samurai blade (it's called blade number 3 because I have uploaded two other sci-fi samurai swords before) modeled, UV unwrapped, and rendered in blender, but textured in substance painter. [USAGE] 

  - This model is suitable for use in Unity, Unreal Engine, Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Movies/Film, Interior/Exterior design, etc 

  - The model was originally modeled in Maya 2020 and rendered with Marmoset Toolbag 4

  - The model is accurate with the real world size and scale

[GENERAL]

  - PBR Materials

  - Game Ready model

  - Low Poly mesh

  - High Poly mesh baked on Low Poly mesh

  - Object pivot points at 0,0,0

  - Object scaled to approximate real world size (cm)

  - Object Height: 103cm

  - Model is fully textured with all materials applied

  - Triangulate mesh and Quad both are included in folder

  - Texture Dimension 2048x2048, 4096x4096 and 8192x8192

[3D Model File Formats]

  - .Ma + .Mb + .Max

  - .3DS + .Fbx + .Obj + .dae + .Abc

  - .unitypackage + .uasset

  - .glTF + .glb + .USD + .USDZ

[GEOMETRY]

  - Polygons: 197

  - Tris: 394

  - Verts: 210

  - The model is accurate with the real world size and scale

[GENERAL]

  - PBR Materials

  - Game Ready model

  - Low Poly mesh

  - High Poly mesh baked on Low Poly mesh

  - Object pivot points at 0,0,0

  - Object scaled to approximate real world size (cm)

  - Model is fully textured with all materials applied

  - Triangulate mesh and Quad both are included in folder

  - Texture Dimension 2048x2048, 4096x4096 and 8192x8192

[3D Model File Formats]

  - .Ma + .Mb + .Max

  - .3DS + .Fbx + .Obj + .dae + .Abc

  - .unitypackage + .uasset

  - .glTF + .glb + .USD + .USDZ

[GEOMETRY]

  - Polygons: 197

  - Tris: 394

description_text:
Created a low poly model of a Katana by using Blender. It's a great piece of a weapon that was used with two hands by samurai in feudal Japan.
This design it different from the traditional Katana because I didn't want it to look like any other Katana. Preview images were rendered with Blender Eevee.
Polygon Count

  - Faces: 14.048

  - Vertices: 14.054

Pack Includede & File Format

  - Blender file v2.93.5 (.blend): Katana.blend

  - FBX file: Katana - FBX

  - OBJ file: Katana - OBJ

  - STL file: Katana - STL

  - ABC file: Katana - ABC

  - DAE file: Katana - DAE

  - glTF file: Katana - glTF

  - Three Materials (Steel for the blade, Gold Steel for the Guard & Wood for the grip)

  - NO Textures

Note: Not printable model and I stongly advice not to purchase it with the intent of printing it.
Enjoy the product and leave a comment.

.mb — Maya (low-poly with UVs)
.png — baked maps (PBR-ready)

Suitable for games, VR/AR, and visualizations
Clean topology, no n-gons, optimized for real-time rendering
Four ready-to-use texture variations + untextured UV-ready version for customization
High-poly version included for baking or rendering

Medieval Viking sword. The textures are made in the Substation Painter and have a resolution of 2K. The model has UVs, textures are packed in .tga format to preserve maximum quality, there are also heightmaps to help achieve maximum quality. Mine is made in Blender.

A cannon (plural: cannon or cannons) is a type of gun classified as artillery that launches a projectile using propellant. In the past, gunpowder was the primary propellant before the invention of smokeless powder in the 19th century. Cannon vary in caliber, range, mobility, rate of fire, angle of fire, and firepower; different forms of cannon combine and balance these attributes in varying degrees, depending on their intended use on the battlefield. The word cannon is derived from several languages, in which the original definition can usually be translated as tube, cane, or reed. In the modern era, the term cannon has fallen into decline, replaced by guns or artillery if not a more specific term such as mortar or howitzer, except for high calibre automatic weapons firing bigger rounds than machine guns, called autocannons

description_text:
Clean model, clean topologysuitable for visualization and for 3D printing.
Akash - New generation (IAST: Ākāśa Sky) abbreviated as Akash-NG is a medium-range mobile surface-to-air missile defense system developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and produced by Bharat Dynamics Limited and Bharat Electronics. Private sector firm Electropneumatics and Hydraulics India is involved in the Development cum Production Partner program.
This missile is a successor to the Akash and Akash-1S series of missiles with improvements such as a Dual-pulse solid rocket motor, a canisterised launcher, and an AESA Multifunction targeting radar to improve its probability of kill with a smaller ground operations and logistics footprint.[6]
The missile uses an Ku-band Active radar seeker which was revealed to the public during Aero India 2021.
As per Electropneumatics and Hydraulics India, Akash NG has range of 70 km and can operate upto an elevation of 20° to 70° with an azimuth of 360°. Two canister missile stacks take 10 minutes to reload. From target acquisition by command-and-control unit, the system can fire one missile within 10 seconds and in 20 seconds a salvo of three missiles can be fired. The deployment time is less than 20 minutes between transportation and ready-to-fire mode.

description_text:
Ultimate USSR Tank Shells Vol.1
This pack includes 6 detailed 125MM USSR Tank shells, including a propellant charge. With PBR textures as well.
  - 3BM-42M
Lekalo (3BM-42M projectile; 3BM-44 projectile assembly)Svinets-1. A brand new round with extremely high elongation tungsten alloy penetrator, utilizing a 4-petal finned composite sabot with two areas of contact, and subcaliber stabilizing fins. This round has a total length of 740mm and so does not fit in traditional T-72 autoloaders. The autoloader upgrade is straightforward and is assumed to have been carried out on newly built T-90 tanks that are therefore compatible with this round. 
  - BM-9
3VBM-3 (3BM-9 projectile; 3BM-10 projectile assembly)The first APFSDS round fielded for the 125mm gun. Represents a scaled-up version of 115mm 3BM-6 APFSDS round with the redesigned tail assembly (5 fins instead of 6 on the 115mm round). The penetrator is made of maraging steel so has a rather modest penetration potential. This, as well as unsatisfactory performance on slanted impacts, delegated the round to practice and trials use; this was also the round initially supplied with the export T-72s and license-produced in several countries.
  - BM-26
3VBM-11 (3BM-26 projectile; 3BM-27 projectile assembly) (DOI 1983)Research topic Nadezhda initiated 1977. The last projectile to follow the BM-12 design principle of a maraging steel body with a small heavy alloy slug to enhance penetration and using steel ring-shaped sabot. Compared to BM-22, reconfigured the AP cap and repositioned the W-C insert to the rear of the projectile body to solve the problems the earlier rounds had with slanted impacts (high ricochet probability). It was also the first round whose development specifically aimed at improving performance against laminate armor arrays present on newly emerging threat armor.
  - BK-14M
This is the Russian 125mm BK-14 (БК-14), a High-Explosive Anti-Tank Fin-Stabilised with Tracer (HEAT-FS-T), setback-armed, impact-fired, piezo-electric initiated, Point-Initiated Base-Detonating (PIBD) projectile, the BK-14M being the same projectile except with a copper Shaped-Charge (SC) cone, intended to defeat armoured targets.
  - OF-19
This is the Russian 125mm OF19  (ОФ19), a high-explosive fragmentation (HE-Frag), fin-stabilised projectile using the OF22 cartridge. In common with the rest of the 125mm ammunition range, the OF19 is a separate loading munition. It is automatically loaded into the breech followed by a semi-combustible propellant case.
  - 4Zh-40
This is the Russian Zh40 (Ж40), a low-explosive projectile propellant charge used with 125mm projectiles entering service in 1962. In common with the 125mm ammunition range, the 125mm APFSDS rounds are all separate loading munitions.

The surprise allowed the attackers to seize the deck of the Lima Barros and Cabral ships, whose crew locked themselves in the towers, but soon the Brazil and Herval corvettes intervened, strafing the occupied decks. The mutiny later formed the basis of Sergei Eisenstein's 1925 silent film The Battleship Potemkin.
After the mutineers sought asylum in Constanța, Romania, and after the Russians recovered the ship, her name was changed to Panteleimon (1905). The screws were not intended for propulsion, but were to aid the two rudders in steering in the confined waters and unpredictable currents of the Mississippi.

HISTORICAL NOTE: The CSS Manassas was an ironclad of the Confederate Navy that was rebuilt from a civil ship. Assigned in 1861, it was purchased in a personal capacity by Captain John A. Stevenson of New Orleans, the ship was converted into a military ship in the port of Algiers, in the state of Louisiana. One of the most curious features of this ship was that its hull was reconverted with a shell style, in addition, its deck was in a very low place to be an easy target for rival ships.
It was placed in the official service in September 1861, the month in which CSS Manassas was taken by the Confederation Navy and officially bought by the Confederate Government in December 1861.
On October 12, 1861, CSS Manassas made his first attack on the unionists. He attacked the unionist force that exercised the Naval blockade on the Mississippi River. The large steam boat known as USS Richmond was rammed and seriously damaged, but did not sink. The CSS Manassas also suffered slight damage in the attack, the damage came due to the very force of its onslaught, yet it was removed and was later successfully repaired.
Specifications:
Type: Steam tug, Ironclad.

HISTORICAL NOTE: Courbet was the lead ship of her class of four dreadnought battleships, the first ones built for the French Navy. She spent the war (1914-1918) in the Mediterranean, where she helped to sink an Austro-Hungarian cruiser, covered the Otranto Barrage that blockaded the Austro-Hungarian Navy in the Adriatic Sea, and often served as a flagship. Although upgraded several times before World War II, she was not considered to be a first-line battleship by the 1930s and spent much of that decade as a gunnery training ship.
Her engines and boilers were removed in 1944 to prepare her for use as a breakwater during the Normandy landings (Operation Neptune) in June 1944. She was scrapped in situ after the war.

HISTORICAL NOTE: The USS Wolverine (IX-64) was a training aircraft carrier used by the United States Navy during World War II. It was originally named Seeandbee and was built as a luxury Great Lakes cruise ship for the Cleveland and Buffalo Transit Company. Seeandbee was launched on November 9, 1912 and was normally used on the route from Cleveland, Ohio to Buffalo, New York.
Seeandbee was acquired by the United States Navy in 1942 and was quickly converted into a freshwater aircraft carrier for the advanced training of naval aviators in carrier take-offs and landings. Renamed USS Wolverine she was not equipped with armor, hangar deck, elevators or armaments. Its propulsion was made by side paddle wheels.
The first aircraft landing on USS Wolverine occurred during September 1942. USS Wolverine along with her sister ship USS Sable was used for the training of 17,000 pilots, landing signal officers and other navy personnel with minimal losses. Following the end of World War II the Navy decommissioned Wolverine on 7 November 1945 and she was sold for scrap in December 1947.

Brazil ordered the ship in 1911 as Rio de Janeiro from the British company Armstrong Whitworth. However, the collapse of the rubber boom in Brazil, led to the sale of the ship under construction to the Ottoman Empire in 1913. The Ottomans renamed their name Sultan Osman I, in honor of the founder of the empire, and the ship was almost ready when World War I broke out. The British government seized it for use by the Royal Navy, along with another Ottoman battleship being built in Britain. Renamed Agincourt by the Royal Navy, she joined the Great Fleet in the North Sea. During the war, he participated in the Battle of Jutland in 1916. Agincourt was placed in reserve in 1919 and sold as scrap in 1922 to comply with the terms of the Washington Naval Treaty.
Additional note: The length of the ship and the huge number of 305mm cannons have always caused huge skepticism in the Royal Navy about the ship's ability to shoot sideways (with all cannons at the same time) without causing structural damage; these doubts were dispelled during the Battle of Jutland, during which the ship fired 144 shots, 84 of which against side fire, silencing its detractors. During this battle, the only one that saw her employed, the ship reported no damage and her crew did not report any deaths or injuries.

description_text: Toy Dragon tank from the movie Dr. NO, first James Bond movie, and two toy soldiers henchmen of Dr. No. This set was meant as an addition to the 1960s Gilbert toy soldiers, so consider that the figures must be printed  at max 8 centimeters tall (I'd say something less because in the movie they are less tall than Connery ). We have no precise blueprints for the dragon, the orignal didn't survive and the one in the Orlando museum is just imagined and made from stills of the movie. My guess is to print it about 22 centimeters in lenght (acccording to your printer's size you may need to slice pieces in two). If you want to put the henchman with the submachine gun in the turret you need to remove the pedestal. There are two tires and an axis so you'll have to print the set twice to get four wheels. Bottom must be inserted carefully and glued, there's an indent to help, but consider that must be set with an orientation of 3 degrees (bottom up and front down). Obviously this is a toy, so you can customize it whatever you like.

The blend files have the textures packed into them, but they are provided as a separate file for the other file formats. The Blend have basic shape keys including blink, brow up, frown, smile, sad, and a rig bone to open the mouth.
I have also provided the Inkscape files I used in making the textures. With these you can easily edit the textures to make new units. Inkscape is a free open source graphic design software.
You can also transpose parts of the different units to another to form entirely new units. They all have the same rig bone structure.
I sincerely hope you find these models useful for your. 
Cheers.

description_text:
I offer a nunchaku - a ninja weapon that is rigged and ready to attack ninja opponents!
The geometry is clean with quads and triangles where convenient. The circles caps are closed with one face, however the use of sharp edges allow to use subdivision with no issues.
The model is textured with 4k textures, including: Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Normal, Height, AO maps. Textures are packed within .blend file but also are included in the archive file.
Normals were baked from a high-poly model that is also included with this package as an .obj file. The low poly model is exported to .obj file and .fbx file with rigging. Every chain link has an individual bone. The rigging can be seen in the preview images. The hinges transfering the movement to the chain are constrain to move properly, following a local rotation axis. Constrains are local-axis dependent, therfore they work properly even when a whole nunchaku, as an objext, is rotated.
The model with armature is exported to .fbx file that can be uploaded to and 3D game engine. If you need a specific format of textures, just message me!
The uv maps do not overlap and each separate piece of the model is unwrapped with seams applied where neccessary.
